chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the person who is unconscious (fainted), he said: 'He repays whatever missed him (of prayers).'

key_terms.الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The person who is unconscious or has fainted
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He repays/makes up (referring to missed prayers)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to make up prayers if I was unconscious or fainting?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via Safwan, establishing that unconsciousness does not exempt one from the obligation of prayer, as the state of *taklif* (legal responsibility) persists. This principle distinguishes between the loss of *awareness* required for valid performance and the loss of *capacity*, ensuring that missed *fard* prayers are fully compensated upon recovery. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for determining the *qada* (make-up) of prayers for those in comas or deep sleep.
